title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
summary: Seasoned chicken thighs are seared until golden, then sliced over penne in a Parmesan cream sauce with cherry tomatoes and spinach. The sauce is loosened with pasta water and finished with lemon juice.

items.original_text: ⅓ cup parmesan, grated, plus more to finish
items.name: Parmesan

items: Season the chicken thighs with the salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, and garlic powder. Sear in the olive oil and 1 tbsp butter over medium-high heat, 5 to 6 minutes per side, until golden and cooked to 165°F (74°C). Set aside to rest.
Boil the penne in salted water 1 minute shy of the package directions. Save some pasta water before draining.
In the same pan, melt the other 1 tbsp butter and cook the garlic for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the cherry tomatoes, tomato purée, Italian seasoning, and chili flakes. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the tomatoes soften and start to burst.
Pour in the chicken stock, scrape up the browned bits, and simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream and simmer gently. Add the spinach and stir until just wilted, then melt in the parmesan until the sauce is smooth and silky.
Stir in the lemon juice, then toss the penne through the sauce with splashes of pasta water until glossy and coated.
Slice the chicken, lay it over the top, finish with extra parmesan, and serve right away.

notes: The written recipe with quantities is the caption on Cooking Whatever's Facebook reel, titled Dinners That Pay My Rent, Episode 6.

flags.text: The source gives a total time of about 35 minutes, but does not break out prep and cook times. The method includes searing 5 to 6 minutes per side, cooking the garlic 30 seconds, cooking the tomatoes 2 to 3 minutes, simmering the stock 2 minutes, and boiling the penne 1 minute shy of the package directions. Those details are in the steps.
The chicken is listed as "2 boneless skinless chicken thighs," with no weight.
The cherry tomatoes are listed as 1/3 cup, halved, with no count.
The method says to boil the penne in salted water; that salt is not listed as a separate ingredient.
The method says to save some pasta water and add it in "splashes" until the sauce is glossy and coated; no amount is given.
The Parmesan is listed as 1/3 cup, grated, plus more to finish; no amount is given for the finishing cheese.
